claims.text: Phase stability in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is governed by a critical threshold in the Gibbs free-energy difference between BCC and FCC phases.
The thermodynamic driving force must overcome kinetic nucleation barriers during cooling for transformation to occur.
When ΔG_BCC-FCC exceeds the critical threshold under a given thermal history, transformation kinetics produce an FCC or mixed phase.
When ΔG_BCC-FCC does not exceed the threshold, the high-temperature BCC phase is retained.
Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is initially in a high-temperature BCC state.
Controlled variation of cooling rates and dwell times near transformation temperatures can test the proposed thermodynamic-kinetic mechanism.
Moderate dwell times allow transformation kinetics to manifest, whereas rapid cooling suppresses them.
Nucleation barriers and local thermal gradients mediate the resulting microstructural phase distribution.
A sufficiently large thermodynamic instability promotes transformation when dwell times permit kinetic processes to proceed.
If kinetic opportunities are insufficient, the metastable high-temperature BCC structure is preserved.
Moderate cooling rates and sufficient dwell near the transformation temperature will increase the FCC or mixed-phase fraction.
Rapid cooling will retain the BCC phase.
The extent of transformation will quantitatively track computed thermodynamic instability combined with measured kinetic delays.
Under the standard moderate-cooling baseline, partial transformation is predicted by simulation and prior experimental trends.
The proposed mechanism is limited to the specified composition and the temperature interval between the high-temperature BCC state and kinetic arrest.
The numerical ΔG_BCC-FCC threshold and nucleation barriers are not yet known and require simulation-experiment calibration.
The hypothesis would be falsified if conditions predicted to exceed the ΔG threshold fail to increase the FCC or mixed-phase fraction.
The hypothesis would also be falsified if rapid cooling produces significant transformation contrary to its predictions.
